assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a routine operation. It is among the most used bond-forming reactions in medicinal and process chemistry, with a conceptually clear catalytic cycle and steady ligand evolution. As a synthetic chemist I regard it as the clearest general method on the list that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds. The 2010 prize covered C-C cross-coupling, so the novelty must be the C-N bond-forming strategy and the ligand design.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled, general catalytic amination after the earlier tin-amide chemistry of Kosugi and Migita. Their credit is the decisive one for generality and practicality, giving a clean two-person prize; Kosugi's precedent is real but is a stoichiometric-tin precursor rather than the general method.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent confirmation, with wide industrial adoption and mechanistic understanding that is stable. Recognition is fully timely, if not overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
How much weight Kosugi's earlier work deserves is an unresolved credit question.
I am relying on my own knowledge of usage and have not verified it against the literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a new mode of reactivity in which radicals and open-shell intermediates are generated under mild conditions, enabling many bond constructions that polar chemistry handles poorly. Its uptake in academic and pharmaceutical synthesis is very broad, and it has merged with nickel and other catalysis. The chemistry is new, not a repackaging of known photochemistry.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over many people (MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson in 2008-2009, with Fukuzumi, Konig, Nicewicz and Melchiorre also credited). A three-person prize is possible but cuts out several credible contributors. MacMillan is already a laureate (2021), which affects willingness to re-award him; the proposal reflects the list's credits, not a settled view.
assessment.maturity: More than a decade of heavy use and confirmation. Some mechanistic questions, such as chain versus non-chain pathways, remain partly open, but the field is clearly mature enough.
uncertainties: Allocation among at least seven credited names is genuinely unresolved.
Whether to include a prior laureate.
Some claims of unique synthetic power may be inflated by the rapid growth of the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization changes the logic of synthesis by treating ubiquitous C-H bonds as functional groups. Ligand- and directing-group-controlled selectivity (Yu) and the Pd(II)/Pd(IV) manifold (Sanford) have been taken up in late-stage functionalization and in total synthesis, where step counts fall. Efficiency in synthesis is exactly the measure I care about.
assessment.attribution: Yu is the leading figure for ligand and template control of site selectivity. Sanford made central contributions to the mechanism and scope of Pd and other metal catalysis. Hartwig's borylation work is crucial for this topic but also overlaps B032, so crediting him twice is a concern. Daugulis and Smith are real contributors, and the three-person limit excludes them.
assessment.maturity: Broad confirmation and adoption, but the field is still moving; industrial use is growing and not yet routine to the degree of cross-coupling. Timing is plausible but could be a few years early.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is a single coherent contribution or several; the title spans ligand, template and borylation chemistry.
Hartwig appears in both B032 and B051.
Practical scale and generality of the most selective systems are still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically precluded acid-base pairs can heterolytically cleave H2 and activate other small molecules without a transition metal. This is a simple, memorable concept that created a new area of main-group catalysis, including metal-free hydrogenation. Practical use in synthesis so far is modest compared with its conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the 2006 H2 activation by a phosphine-borane and developed the concept; Erker made decisive contributions through intramolecular systems and substrate scope. A two-person prize is clean and fair on the supplied credits.
assessment.maturity: Nearly twenty years of broad independent confirmation, but industrial application remains limited. Recognition would reward concept over uptake, so I weigh it below the cross-coupling-type methods.
uncertainties: Limited use outside academia.
Whether the catalytic scope has lived up to the early expectations.
Earlier related observations (e.g. Brown, Tochtermann) may complicate priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (imidazol-2-ylidenes, and cyclic alkyl amino carbenes) showed that a species long thought too reactive can be a bottle-stable reagent. N-heterocyclic carbenes became ubiquitous ligands (e.g. in olefin metathesis catalysts) and organocatalysts, so the impact on molecule-making is wide.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand (1988 phosphinocarbene) and Arduengo (1991 crystalline NHC) are the pioneers; Nolan is the leading figure for NHC-metal catalysis. This choice does not credit Bode and Rovis, who are organocatalysis contributors, as I consider the discovery of the isolable carbene the core.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of confirmation, with extensive use in catalysis. The metathesis connection was partly recognized in 2005, which may make the committee cautious about double recognition.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should treat isolation (Arduengo, Bertrand) and the ligand/catalysis applications (Nolan) together.
Overlap with the 2005 metathesis prize.
The Bertrand versus Arduengo priority question is a matter of interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptide segments, so that synthetic and semisynthetic proteins of useful size are practical. It changed protein chemistry, enabling the incorporation of non-natural residues, modifications and probes, and is widely used. The chemical idea (thioester exchange followed by S-to-N acyl shift) is simple and clearly new.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed the original reaction in 1994; Muir extended it to expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are credible contributors to later improvements, so the list is wider than three.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use and confirmation, with growing impact in therapeutic protein manufacture. Recognition is mature, though some may judge the impact more specialist than that of the leading synthetic methods.
uncertainties: Whether the field would regard the work as chemistry at the border with chemical biology.
Credit among Kent, Dawson and Muir versus later contributors is unresolved.
Industrial scale impact is smaller than for small-molecule methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: RAFT polymerization offers living or controlled radical polymerization with great functional-group tolerance and a very broad monomer range, so complex polymer architectures can be made with simple chemistry. Industrial and academic use is large. This is polymer synthesis rather than my own field, and I view it as less conceptually deep than organometallic discoveries.
assessment.attribution: The CSIRO team (Rizzardo, Moad, Thang) developed the RAFT process in 1998, with the dithioester chain-transfer agents and a mechanism understood. The credit is a clean three-person configuration. It competes with ATRP (B069) in the same area, so only one is likely to be recognised.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of confirmation and well-established use. Timely, but a recognition for controlled radical polymerization would need to choose between RAFT, ATRP and NMP.
uncertainties: Competition with ATRP for the same prize.
Whether the committee would regard the progress as incremental over living radical polymerization.
Polymer expertise is outside my own field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors change single DNA bases by chemical deamination on a Cas-guided scaffold, without double-strand breaks. The chemical idea is real (engineering of deaminases, uracil glycosylase inhibition) and has clear therapeutic potential. As an organic chemist, I ask what was new chemically; the adenine base editor, which required evolving a deaminase that acts on DNA, is a striking piece of molecular engineering.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the work; Komor developed the cytosine base editor and Gaudelli the adenine base editor as first authors. Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) were independent and parallel. A Liu-led trio is defensible but a Liu-only or Liu-plus-one configuration would be alternatives.
assessment.maturity: Introduced in 2016-2017, so it has less time depth than other candidates, though clinical trials are now under way. It may be premature relative to the methodology options above, and the CRISPR prize in 2020 already acknowledged genome editing.
uncertainties: Early to judge long-term clinical outcomes.
Overlap with the 2020 genome-editing prize and with B026 (prime editing).
Fair credit for the parallel Target-AID work.
